newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Sixty pct of Ukraine economy now in shadow - expert.
newsitem.headline: Sixty pct of Ukraine economy now in shadow - expert.

text.p: Ukraine's shadow economy has expanded to account for 60 percent of all economic activity, up from previous estimates of 40 percent, a Ukrainian economic expert said on Wednesday.
"More than 60 percent of the economy is now in the shadow," Olexander Razumkov, chief of the Ukrainian Centre for Economic and Political Research, told politicians and economists.
"The government has no influence in this area."
President Leonid Kuchma, in his state of the nation address last week, said the shadow economy had grown from 35-40 percent to account for 52-55 percent of economic activity.
Ukraine reported a 10 percent drop in the official gross domestic product (GDP) last year.

"Calculations show the drop in gross domestic product, when including the shadow economy, was no more than two to four percent, and there was no drop whatsoever in the industrial sector," Kuchma said.
Ukraine's parliament is reviewing a package to reform the tax system, where high rates and inconsistencies have been blamed for forcing business activity underground.
The package will underpin the 1997 budget, already nearly three months late, which parliament is due to debate next month.
Acceptance of the budget could pave the way for receipt of a $2.5 to $3 billion International Monetary Fund credit.
